Where Ollama Stores Models and How to Move Them

Ollama defaults to ~/.ollama/models on Mac, %USERPROFILE%\.ollama\models on Windows, and /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models for the standard Linux service. To use another drive, stop the server, copy the full model folder, set OLLAMA_MODELS for the server, then restart and run a copied model before removing the original.

  1. Find the active models folder
  2. Prepare a copy
  3. macOS
  4. Windows
  5. Linux systemd
  6. Docker
  7. Verify the copy and roll back
  8. See the offline migration test

Find the active Ollama models folder

Find the machine and process serving your requests. If OLLAMA_HOST points at another machine, inspect that machine’s configuration. A shell variable you set for the client cannot tell you what an already-running server uses.

InstallationDefault model folder
macOS app or local CLI~/.ollama/models in the server user’s home
Windows app%USERPROFILE%\.ollama\models
Linux terminal server~/.ollama/models in the server user’s home
Standard Linux systemd service/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models
Official Docker example/root/.ollama/models inside the container, under its named volume

If you previously changed the path, inspect the server’s OLLAMA_MODELS setting or launch configuration first. For a local model, ollama show --modelfile MODEL:TAG can also show a FROM path inside the active store. Substitute an installed tag and use the path only when the output contains a local file. For Docker check the mount that provides that path.

Copy the whole store before switching paths

  1. Save the output of ollama list. Note the full tags you need, including custom ones. Keep any original GGUF and Modelfile used to import a custom model.
  2. Confirm the new disk is mounted and has room for the complete folder. Create a dedicated, empty destination. Use a filesystem that preserves the store’s files and links.
  3. Wait for active requests to finish and stop the Ollama server. Copy the contents of the model folder together, preserving their directory structure and links. A blobs-only copy does not preserve the tags. Keep the original folder until the new copy passes the checks below.

Move Ollama models on macOS

Quit the Ollama app from the menu bar, or stop the terminal that is running ollama serve. The example uses the default source and a mounted drive called AI SSD. Replace both locations if yours differ. Make sure the drive is mounted before creating the folder.

new="/Volumes/AI SSD/ollama-models"
mkdir -p "$new"
rsync -a "$HOME/.ollama/models/" "$new/"

After the copy succeeds, set the path for the app.

launchctl setenv OLLAMA_MODELS "$new"

Reopen the app. For a terminal-managed server, use OLLAMA_MODELS="$new" ollama serve in the same shell instead of the launchctl step. The launchctl setenv setting applies to the current login session. Recheck it after a reboot and confirm the path after reconnecting the drive. For a terminal server, keep the setting in the command or script that starts it.

Move Ollama models to another drive on Windows

  1. Quit Ollama from the notification area. In Explorer, copy all contents of %USERPROFILE%\.ollama\models to an empty folder on the destination drive, for example D:\Ollama\models. Check for copy errors.
  2. Open Edit environment variables for your account. Under user variables set OLLAMA_MODELS to the full destination folder path.
  3. Open Ollama from the Start menu. If the drive letter changed, resolve that before restarting the app.

If you run Ollama inside WSL, apply the appropriate Linux instructions inside that environment.

Move the models of a Linux systemd service

These commands assume the standard ollama service account and an already-mounted disk at /mnt/ai. Substitute the actual source if it was customized. The destination below is a dedicated model store.

sudo systemctl stop ollama.service
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ai/ollama-models
sudo rsync -a /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models/ /mnt/ai/ollama-models/
sudo chown -R ollama:ollama /mnt/ai/ollama-models
sudo systemctl edit ollama.service

Run the copy and ownership steps successfully before setting this override. The service account needs access to the destination and must be able to traverse its parent folders.

[Service]
Environment="OLLAMA_MODELS=/mnt/ai/ollama-models"
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start ollama.service

If you start ollama serve yourself, set the variable for that process as shown in the macOS terminal example, using the Linux destination path.

Move the model store used by an Ollama container

Use docker inspect ollama --format '{{json .Mounts}}' to see the mount used by the server. In Ollama’s official Docker example, ollama:/root/.ollama mounts the named volume ollama. If you already configured a separate model directory, use its actual container path in the commands below.

For the default example, stop the original container and copy the contents from it into an existing empty folder on the new drive. docker cp can read a stopped container. Ensure the destination can preserve links and is accessible to Docker.

docker stop ollama
docker cp ollama:/root/.ollama/models/. /mnt/ai/ollama-models/

Add /mnt/ai/ollama-models:/models as a bind mount and set OLLAMA_MODELS=/models in the container configuration. Recreate the service with its existing image, ports, devices and other settings. Keep the old volume attached at its original location if it holds other Ollama data, and keep the source until verification. Run docker exec ollama ollama list against the replacement container.

Check the migrated tags and roll back if they’re missing

  1. Run ollama list on the restarted server and compare it with the saved list. To compare exact model contents, save and compare the digest values from GET /api/tags before and after.
  2. Use an already-listed local tag in ollama run MODEL:TAG and send a short prompt. For Docker use docker exec -it ollama ollama run MODEL:TAG. Test the custom or most important tags before deleting the original. Do not run a missing tag to validate the copy, since Ollama may download the model again and hide the problem.
  3. If the new list is empty or the model fails to load, stop the server. Confirm the path is set for that server, the disk is mounted, and the copied folder contains both weights and tag information at the expected level. Restore the previous setting and restart if you need to return to the original store. If you were using the default, clear the variable instead. On macOS use launchctl unsetenv OLLAMA_MODELS for the app. For systemd or a container, revert the specific override or mount you changed.

Keep the old path until the new store also works after a restart. If you installed or changed models after the switch, keep a copy of the new store before rolling back so those changes remain recoverable. To remove just one obsolete tag, delete the model through Ollama.

What happened when we switched stores offline

On macOS arm64, we restarted Ollama 0.40.18 four times against isolated directories. The source was a local import of Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M. Both Ollama and the test client could reach loopback only, with Ollama cloud disabled.

Store usedInstalled tagsGeneration result
Original1HTTP 200, LOCAL_OK
Empty destination0HTTP 404, model missing
Copied destination, original path absent1Same digest and reply
Switched back to original1Same digest and reply

We compared file hashes and link targets after the copy, then made the original path unavailable for the destination test. This verifies one model using a macOS CLI server. The app, Windows, Linux systemd and Docker instructions are based on documentation.
